sourceNote: All records curated from Wikipedia articles and publicly documented sources. Dharamshala destination includes the McLeod Ganj area (5km uphill, same municipality since 2013). McLeod Ganj is an alias of the dharamshala destination — NOT a separate child destination. Places in the McLeod Ganj area are correctly included here. Destination center: 32.219, 76.3234 (lower Dharamshala). All records needs_review.

places.name: Tsuglagkhang Complex
places.description: The main temple complex of the Tibetan exile community in McLeod Ganj, housing the official residence of the 14th Dalai Lama. The complex includes the Tsuglagkhang Cathedral (the main temple with a 2.5m gilded Shakyamuni Buddha), Kalachakra Temple (with large thangka murals), and a Tibet Museum documenting Tibetan history and the 1950 Chinese occupation. The Dalai Lama's residence (Namgyal Monastery) is adjacent. Core of the Tibetan government-in-exile's spiritual life. Free entry to the temple complex; museum has a small fee.

places.name: Namgyal Monastery
places.description: Personal monastery of the Dalai Lama, established at McLeod Ganj after 1959, with 200+ resident monks. The monastery focuses on Tibetan ritual practice and tantric studies. Monks can be seen debating in the courtyard. The attached Namgyal Institute of Buddhist Dialectics is a leading centre for Tibetan scholarship. Open to respectful visitors. Located within the Tsuglagkhang complex; usually visited alongside the main temple.

places.name: Tibet Museum, McLeod Ganj
places.description: Museum documenting Tibetan history, culture, and the 1950 Chinese annexation of Tibet, operated by the Tibet Heritage Fund inside the Tsuglagkhang complex. Permanent exhibitions cover traditional Tibetan life, the mass flight of Tibetan refugees in 1959, and the ongoing Tibet issue through photographs, maps, and audio-visual displays. One of the most informative introductions to Tibetan history outside Tibet. Nominal entry fee. Closed Mondays.

places.name: Bhagsu Waterfall
places.description: Popular waterfall reached via a 2km trail from McLeod Ganj through Bhagsu village. The trail passes the ancient Bhagsunag Shiva Temple (free) before ascending to the falls, which cascade down a cliff face into a pool. The area is heavily visited in summer; the trail to a second, higher set of falls (Shiva Cafe area) offers solitude for those willing to climb further. Free to visit the falls; the trail begins in the village of Bhagsu.

places.name: Triund Trek
places.description: Most popular day trek from McLeod Ganj, ending at Triund meadow at 2828m — a high ridge with 270° views of the Dhauladhar snow range. Trail begins at Gallu Devi Temple (1890m) and climbs 5km through oak and rhododendron forest before opening onto the ridge. Return takes 3–4 hours up, 2–3 hours down. Snow possible Oct–Apr. Camping at the top permitted (tent hire available on-site in season). Registration at the Gallu Devi gate; small fee applies in season.
places.area: Above McLeod Ganj, trail from Gallu Devi
places.openingDays: Open year-round; challenging Nov–Mar due to snow

places.name: Norbulingka Institute
places.description: Centre for traditional Tibetan arts and crafts established in 1988 at Sidhpur, 5km below McLeod Ganj. Set in beautifully landscaped Tibetan-style gardens, the campus houses workshops producing thangkas (scroll paintings), appliqué, sculpture, woodcarving, and traditional costumes — all using techniques preserved from pre-occupation Tibet. Gallery and shop sell craft works; visitors can observe artisans at work. The on-site Losel Doll Museum displays dressed dolls depicting Tibetan regional dress and ceremonies.

places.name: Dharamshala Cricket Stadium
places.description: HPCA Cricket Stadium at 1457m, one of the highest cricket grounds in the world and considered one of the most scenic. Backed by the snow-capped Dhauladhar range, the stadium hosts IPL and international matches. Non-match-day visits are possible (entry to view the ground from outside on match days; stadium tours may be available). The venue became internationally famous after the 2016 ICC WT20 match. Located in lower Dharamshala between town and McLeod Ganj.
places.openingDays: Viewable from road anytime; internal access varies by match schedule

places.name: St. John in the Wilderness Church
places.description: Neo-Gothic Anglican church (1852) in the forests between lower Dharamshala and McLeod Ganj. Built by the British Army during the early colonial period in Kangra valley. Notable for its stained glass windows and as the burial site of Lord Elgin, Viceroy of India, who died at Dharamshala in 1863. The churchyard has colonial-era graves. Surrounded by tall deodar trees giving it a distinctly atmospheric setting. Still holds occasional services. Free to visit.
places.area: Forsyth Ganj, forest between Dharamshala and McLeod Ganj

places.name: Kangra Fort
places.description: One of the oldest and largest forts in the Himalayan foothills, 20km south of Dharamshala in Kangra town. The fort dates from the pre-common era Katoch dynasty and has been held by the Maurya, Mughal, Sikh, and British empires. It was largely destroyed by the 1905 Kangra earthquake but remains impressive in scale. ASI-protected; paid entry. On a rocky promontory above the Baner and Manjhi rivers. The adjacent Brajeshwari Devi Temple (one of the 51 Shakti Peethas) is free and can be visited together.

places.name: Masrur Rock-cut Temples
places.description: 8th-century rock-cut Hindu temple complex cut from a single sandstone outcrop, 32km southwest of Dharamshala, in the Beas valley foothills. The early medieval Pratihara-period temples are dedicated to Shiva, Vishnu, and Devi; carved in a style combining Kashmiri and Gupta-Himachali influences. Severely damaged by the 1905 Kangra earthquake. A largely unknown ASI site with almost no tourist infrastructure, making it one of the most rewarding undiscovered monuments in Himachal Pradesh. ASI entry fee.

places.name: Dal Lake Dharamshala
places.description: Small picturesque lake at 1457m near Naddi village, 3km above McLeod Ganj, surrounded by deodar forest. A cedar grove on the western shore hosts an annual October fair (Shivratri Mela). Considerably smaller and more peaceful than Dal Lake in Srinagar. The lake has a Devi temple on its shore. A popular short walk from McLeod Ganj; views of Dhauladhar range in good weather. Paddle boats available seasonally. Free to visit the lakeside.

places.name: Library of Tibetan Works and Archives
places.description: Principal repository of Tibetan cultural and religious knowledge outside Tibet, established 1970 under the Tibetan government-in-exile. Holds over 90,000 manuscripts, texts, and documents in Tibetan, Sanskrit, and other languages, plus thangkas, statues, and ritual objects. The reading room and public exhibitions are open to visitors. The LTWA runs Tibetan language and Buddhism courses for international students. Located in lower McLeod Ganj (Gangchen Kyishong, the government-in-exile campus). Nominal entry fee.

places.name: McLeod Ganj Tibetan Kitchen
places.description: McLeod Ganj is Dharamshala's Tibetan-in-exile hub, making it home to some of India's best momos, thukpa, and tsampa. Tibetan Kitchen restaurant near the Dalai Lama temple is a community staple. Try gyathuk (clear broth noodles) and sha momo (steamed meat dumplings).

places.name: Dharamshala Kangra Chai Culture
places.description: The Kangra Valley below Dharamshala grows Himachal Pradesh's own tea. Local chai stalls near the cricket ground and bazaar offer spiced Kangra tea — distinct from Darjeeling with its own flavour profile. Pair with a Himachali snack like madra or babru (black gram stuffed bread).
